en-US.author: David Štencl and Ondřej Šumbera
en-US.description: Capture your screen, convert, and edit video and sound in one desktop app.
en-US.longDescription: ClipHearth is a desktop media workbench for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It takes screenshots you can mark up and find by their text, records your screen, microphone, and camera, and its built-in browser finds the video or sound playing on a page, including live streams and internet radio, which it can also record at a set time. The Converter turns files into 11 video and 9 audio formats, in batches or under a target size. The Editor cuts a video by editing its text and takes out pauses and ehms; its timeline lays out the camera, titles, zooms, chapters, and every sound track. It burns in word-by-word captions, makes vertical clips and App Store previews, adds music, a logo, and clean-up, and splits the result into parts, always as a new file. Following brings in new podcast episodes on its own, and a shared box sends files between your computers, encrypted end to end. Both come with the license, as does the optional AI that runs on your computer. ClipHearth is for media you own or are authorized to keep and does not circumvent DRM. Try it free for 3 tasks; screenshots and screen recordings up to 3 minutes stay free for good.
en-US.name: ClipHearth
en-US.releaseNotes:
- The Editor lays out a screen recording with its camera part by part. On the timeline's Layout row the camera sits in the corner, fills the picture, stands side by side with the screen or leaves for a while, and each change fades over.
- The Text row of the timeline puts words, a title card or a picture over part of the video. Each one fades or slides in and out, and the preview shows it as the export will.
- Behind me sets what is behind you in a recording with the camera, also after recording. Keep the room as recorded, or put the screen, a picture or the room blurred behind you. Nothing leaves your computer.
- Join can fade the clips into each other or go through black between them.
- Chapters go on the timeline, and a file's own chapters come along. The export keeps them in their places after every cut, and Copy for YouTube copies them in YouTube's format.
- Zooms are blocks on the timeline. Each one zooms in, moves on to more places quickly or gliding, and zooms out again.
- A screen recording with zooms or a camera keeps its screen and its camera beside the video. The Editor opens it with them, so the zooms and the camera can still be changed.
- AI subtitles save .srt, .vtt or both, and the words as text in .txt or .md. Words it should know helps them spell names and terms.
- Even out the loudness has three targets, Podcast, Video sites and Broadcast. The Editor can also save in H.265, which keeps the quality in a smaller file.
- Music added in the Editor goes quieter under the speech by itself, and you choose how much.
- The Editor exports an App Store preview at Apple's size and a GIF that stays under the size you set. Fast trim without re-encoding saves a trimmed part in seconds.
- Settings can name an edited or a converted file after your own pattern, with its name, its number in a batch and the date.
- Record a stream at a set time records a radio programme or a live broadcast on its own, once, every day, on weekdays or every week.
- On Windows with Intel graphics, a video that had dropped frames came out with some frames up to a second late. Every frame now stays in place.
- On 32-bit Windows a live broadcast with a picture can be recorded again, music that plays on over the cuts no longer stops the export, and MKV and WebM files keep their sound exactly in place.
- The Converter keeps a sound track that starts after the picture exactly in its place in MP4 and MOV.
